jobs.text: Commercial tea-growing began near Sylhet in the 1850s, and today the region has well over a hundred gardens. The pickers, often descended from families brought from other parts of India generations ago, still pluck “two leaves and a bud” by hand. Tea workers earn low wages, and improving them is a long-running public debate.

jobs.text: A haor is a bowl-shaped wetland that stays dry in winter and becomes a lake in the rainy season. Farmers grow one big rice crop, called boro, in the dry months, and fishers take over when the water rises. Early floods in April can wash away the ripening rice, so families watch the sky closely.
jobs.alt: A haor is a bowl-shaped wetland that stays dry in winter and becomes a lake in the rainy season.

jobs.text: Hazrat Shah Jalal is remembered as a Sufi saint who travelled to Sylhet in the early fourteenth century and is honoured across Bengal. His shrine in the city is a place of prayer and gathering, and visitors often feed pigeons and offer food to the poor there. Sylhet is sometimes called the city of saints.
